subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should memory-lancedb expose raw UUIDs in `memory_recall` content as the supported deletion selector, use an opaque/confirmable handle, or wait for the broader memory lifecycle contract?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent deletion handle and conflicting-fact lifecycle affect durable user memory, auditability, plugin API expectations, and future soft-delete/tombstone behavior.

options.title: Expose recall UUIDs now
options.body: Add model-visible UUIDs to `memory_recall` rows, preserve UUID validation in `memory_forget`, and leave replacement/deprecation semantics to the broader lifecycle tracker.

options.title: Design opaque handles first
options.body: Pause narrow repair until maintainers define a safer model-visible deletion handle or confirmation flow that does not expose durable storage IDs.

options.title: Route only to lifecycle MVP
options.body: Treat this as fully owned by the broader memory review/edit/forget/conflict design and do not land a standalone recall handoff fix.

recommendation.title: Expose recall UUIDs now
recommendation.body: Add model-visible UUIDs to `memory_recall` rows, preserve UUID validation in `memory_forget`, and leave replacement/deprecation semantics to the broader lifecycle tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is memory lifecycle and storage contract direction, and current related history points most strongly to this area owner.
